title: Riemann Hypothesis over Finite Holographic Substrate

rows.label: A1
rows.predicate: The framed substrate: the Carrier $\F_\Omega$, $\Omega=4\dS+1$, the Subject $\Fp(\chron;0,1,\gen)$, $\p=4\kp+1$, with $\pi=2\kp$, $\im=\gen^{-\kp}$, $\E=\gen^{\,\im}$; the four cardinal domains, labelled in the Carrier register (space, time, momentum, energy) and read by the Subject as counts (wavenumber, frequency); the orbital sphere with its latitudes, the shell Fourier transform on the phase cycle; time as scale-dilation.

rows.label: A2
rows.predicate: Finitude: for any reading of capacity $R$ the registered Universe embeds in the shell of $R$ members, and among $R+1$ members two share a residue; the totality is finite, its cardinality $\Omega$. A theorem of the master ledger (00:A2), proved in the core, cited as the closure's first premise (F7).

rows.label: A3
rows.predicate: Completeness: whatever exists is registered within, the registration of any totality being onto its registered Universe, so there is no outside and no host; two totalities each registered whole within the other have one count. A theorem of the master ledger (00:A3), proved in the core; cited by Definition~\ref{def:existence} (D12).

rows.label: A4
rows.predicate: Observation: every observation is a registration by an embedded part of $o<\Omega$ states; every reading identifies two members, and a complete reading needs the whole count; one translation carries each member to each. A theorem of the master ledger (00:A4), proved in the core, cited as the closure's second premise (F7).

rows.label: A5
rows.predicate: The Carrier: a timeless torsor of $\Omega$ elements, its cardinality its only absolute characteristic; reframings $x\mapsto ax+b$ are automorphisms, so $0$, $1$, $-1$ are frame data; a Subject's frame charts it as the prime field $\F_\Omega$, never the Carrier (00:A6). A finite holographic substrate: capacity $\dS$ the horizon entropy, $\Omega=4\dS+1$ its exact content (00:A7, 10:A2), the Subject embedded under $\p^{2}<\Omega$.

rows.label: A6
rows.predicate: The classical apparatus, as the chart of Theorem~\ref{thm:hp}: the explicit formula $\psi(x)=x-\sum_\rho x^{\rho}/\rho-\dots$, the logarithmic derivative $-\zeta'/\zeta(s)=\sum\Lambda(n)n^{-s}$, the Riemann--Siegel length $\sqrt{T/2\pi}$ as the scale of the window; the first zeros to twelve digits from the primes alone by harmonic inversion; the dilation generator $-i(x\partial_x+\tfrac12)$ of Berry--Keating with the heights as its generalised eigenvalues [chart].

rows.label: A8
rows.predicate: The chart's known off-line case: the Davenport--Heilbronn series, a Dirichlet series with the functional equation and no Euler product, has marks off the line, the first pair at $0.8085171825+85.6993484854\,i$ and $1-\bar s$ [chart]. The paper claims nothing about the marks of a chart function.

blocks.title: The shell: the frames, the primes, the modes, the critical line and its circle

rows.label: B1
rows.predicate: The two frames and their alignment: the Carrier chart $\F_\Omega$, held by no embedded observer, and the Subject $\Fp$, $\p^{2}<\Omega$; shared: the unit and the rules of arithmetic, agreeing on the window, the Subject's residues the Carrier's below $\p$, whence the half-turn and the conjugation; not shared: generator, $\eta$; the cycles share the core $Q_4$, not a clock ($12\nmid232$).

rows.label: B2
rows.predicate: Frame coincidence below the horizon: for $n\le\sqrt \p$ the residue $n$ is the same integer in $\Fp$ and $\F_\Omega$, and primality of $n$ equals irreducibility in the Subject chart; the Subject-realised primes $\Pi_\p$ are the primes to $\sqrt \p$. A prime is a label on the prime meridian below the horizon.

rows.label: B3

rows.label: B4

rows.label: B5
rows.predicate: Slot complementarity: $\Phi(k)=-\gen^{\,k}$ bijects the nontrivial spectral slots onto the nonterminal additive slots $\Fx{\Omega}\setminus\{-1\}$, the two removed points being $\mu_2$, the intertwiner the half-cycle element.

rows.label: B6

rows.label: B14

blocks.title: The dual and the drive: the shell theorem, the parity, the explicit formula, the spectrum

rows.label: E12
rows.predicate: \textbf{The shell theorem.} On every shell, for every vector, in $\Fp$: (i) the dual $\hat v(k)=\sum v(x)x^{k}$ inverts exactly, $v(y)=-\sum\hat v(k)y^{-k}$, the constant mode the mean term; (ii) the Parseval identity (E13); (iii) every mode on the critical line, an eigenvector of the drive (E15); (iv) the parity and (v) the explicit formula along the meridian (E14).
rows.source: Thm.~\ref{thm:hp}\newline \pywit{rh}{p20043}{E12}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p20043}{E12}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p20043}{E12} \lean{Rh.chi\_inversion, Rh.chi\_shift, Rh.scale\_shift, FRC.Rh.shift\_power\_character, FRC.Rh.shift\_trace, Rh.readout\_on\_line, Rh.readout\_slot\_index, FRC.Rh.Ext.readout\_on\_line, FRC.Rh.Ext.readout\_slot\_index, FRC.Horizon.mode\_expansion, FRC.Horizon.inversion\_res}

rows.label: E13
rows.predicate: The Parseval identity: $\sum_k\hat v(k)\hat v(-k)=-\sum_x v(x)^{2}$ on every shell, the finite Parseval identity of the cycle with the self-pairing $-1$ in place of the complex norm; in the chart the $\p-1$ complex characters are an orthogonal basis with $\lVert\chi_j\rVert^{2}=\p-1$ and the same identity reads $\sum_j|\hat v_{\mathbb C}(j)|^{2}=(\p-1)\sum|v|^{2}$ [chart].

rows.label: E14
rows.predicate: The parity and the explicit formula: (iv) $W^{2}=-J$, $F^{2}=J$, $F^{4}=1$, the half-turn $k\mapsto k+\pi$ on the line; (v) for every vector and every $x\le\p-1$, $\sum_{y\le x}v(y)=-\sum_k\hat v(k)S_k(x)$ with $S_k(x)=\sum_{y\le x}y^{-k}$ and $S_0(x)=x$, along the meridian, from the inversion on the residues with the self-pairing $-1$.

rows.label: E15
rows.predicate: \textbf{The drive theorem.} The drive $(Dv)(x)=v(\gen x)$ permutes the residues, orthogonal for the pairing of E12 (i); its eigenvectors are the modes $x^{k}$ and their nonzero multiples, eigenvalue $\gen^{k}$, the spectrum $\Fx{\p}$, simple, in $\Fp$, the modes isotropic for $k\ne0,\pi$; the readout is minus the eigenvalue; the half-turn negates it; at a shared label both frames' modes have eigenvalue $-\theta$ (B13).
rows.source: Thm.~\ref{thm:drive}\newline \pywit{rh}{p20094}{E15}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p20094}{E15} \lean{FRC.Rh.shift\_power\_character, FRC.Horizon.drive\_orthogonal, FRC.Horizon.spectrum\_simple, FRC.Horizon.readout\_eigen, FRC.Horizon.half\_turn\_negates, FRC.Horizon.modes\_isotropic}

rows.label: F9
rows.predicate: The exhibit [chart]: the prime-power labels of the windows of depth $13$, $39$, $173$, read along the chart's height, put their five tallest peaks on $10$ to $36$ at the first five classical heights, within $2\pi/\log H$; Subject and Carrier windows agree within the Subject's; at depth $10^{6}$ the ten tallest on $10$ to $52$ are the ten heights, within $0.05$.

rows.label: F10
rows.predicate: \textbf{No zero off the line.} Under B1, D11, D12: the registered lines are the prime meridian and the critical line (B9); the Subject's zeros that exist are its nontrivial modes on the critical line, each the Carrier's zero at that label (B13); a point off both lines is on no registered line, and no embedded frame's reading of it exists.

legend.text: Derived within the framework from the rows above it, or an exact instance check in integer arithmetic; a predicate whose content is a chart computation carries its figures as declared [chart] and is a theorem in the weaker sense that the linked witness reproduces them on the stated instances --- the closing paragraph lists the two grades separately.

A2.name: FRC.Foundation.registered_finite
A2.doc: 20:A2, A2 — the registered Universe is finite: whatever the totality `U`, what a reading of capacity `R` registers of it embeds in the shell of `R` members. No finiteness of `U` is assumed; the bound is the reading's, a record being finite (29:C1).

A2.name: FRC.Foundation.no_unlimited_supply
A2.doc: 20:A2, A2 — no reading registers an unlimited supply: among any `R + 1` members of the totality, a reading of capacity `R` gives two the same residue, found by search (the pigeonhole `FRC.Logic.no_mirror`, 5:C2; the idleness of the unbounded supply, 29:C2).

A2.name: FRC.Foundation.agent_bound
A2.doc: 20:A2, A2 — the agent's bound, the row's instance at capacity `R = records s K` (29:C1): a shell read whole — injectively — into the records of an agent of capacity `K` over `s ≥ 2` symbols has at most `records s K` members, fewer than `s^(K+1)` (`complete_needs_whole` at `o = records s K`, `records_lt`; 5:C2). The row's finitude clauses are `registered_finite` and `no_unlimited_supply` above; the structural cardinality Ω is A7's, consumed.

A3.name: FRC.Foundation.registration_onto
A3.doc: 20:A3, A3 — whatever exists is registered within: the registration of any totality is onto its registered Universe (the definition of `Registered` read back: every residue has a member). The row's "no outside, no host" is A8's and A1's, consumed by reference, not this theorem's: the conjunct holds on a shell read inside a larger host.

A3.name: FRC.Foundation.mutual_registration_count
A3.doc: 20:A3, A3 — two totalities each registered whole within the other have one count: injections both ways between shells force `m = n` (the pigeonhole `FRC.Logic.no_mirror`, 5:C2, both ways). With A6, one count is one Carrier. Silent on a host: a shell with more points registers a shell with fewer.

A4.name: FRC.Foundation.observer_part
A4.doc: 20:A4, A4 (Observation, first clause) — a bounded observer is a proper part: an observer with `o < Ω` states holds no injective encoding of the Carrier's `Ω` points, and every reading `ρ` into its states identifies two distinct points (the pigeonhole, `FRC.Logic.no_mirror`; 25:D1, 5:C2). The two points are found by search.

A4.name: FRC.Foundation.complete_needs_whole
A4.doc: 20:A4, A4 (Observation, second clause) — a complete reading needs the whole count: a reading of the `Ω` points into `o` records that identifies no two points has `Ω ≤ o` (the contrapositive of `observer_part`). A reader that is not the whole reads incompletely.

A4.name: FRC.Foundation.translation_torsor
A4.doc: 20:A4, A4 (Observation, third clause) — the Carrier is a translation torsor (A6): exactly one translation carries each member to each. The origin is frame data: the shell's `0` is the chart's, and the translation carrying `0` to `x` makes `x` an origin as good; the affine frames are a torsor under the frame group (1:C2, `simply_transitive`).

B9.name: FRC.Horizon.invariant_lines
B9.doc: 20:B9, 20:F10, the invariant-line form — the affine lines of the extension are `H_b = {Im z = b}` (`p` lines) and `S_{c,a} = {Re z = a + c·Im z}` (`p²` lines). Conjugation keeps `H_b` exactly when `b = 0` (the meridian) and `S_{c,a}` exactly when `c = 0` (the lines of direction `η`); the half-turn keeps `H_b` exactly when `b = 0` and `S_{c,a}` exactly when `a = 2⁻¹` (the lines through the centre). Hence a line kept by both is the meridian `H_0` or the critical line `S_{0,2⁻¹}`: exactly two.

B12.name: FRC.Horizon.drive_on_line

B12.name: FRC.Horizon.reflection_on_line

B13.name: FRC.Horizon.critical_line
B13.doc: 20:B8, 20:B9, 20:B13 — the finite critical line: `Tr z = 1` exactly when `Re z = 2⁻¹ = 2κ + 1`; it is the fixed locus of `σ = ρ ∘ φ`; every `2⁻¹ + bη` lies on it, one point per residue `b` — `p` points.

B13.name: FRC.Horizon.zero_slot
B13.doc: 20:B4, 20:B13, Z10 — the finite zeta on every shell: over the nonzero residues `x = l + 1`, `l < p − 1`, `Σ x^k = 0` for every nonterminal exponent `0 < k < p − 1`, and `Σ x^{p−1} = −1` on the full cycle.

B13.name: FRC.Horizon.mode_at_label
B13.doc: 20:B13, 20:F10 — every label other than `0` and `−1` is the readout of a nontrivial mode: `θ ≠ 0, −1` is `−g^k` for some `1 ≤ k ≤ p − 2`; the label `−1` carries the constant mode `k = 0` and `0` is the centre.

B13.name: FRC.Horizon.line_coincidence_all
B13.doc: 20:B13, 20:F10 — frame coincidence on the critical line for every zero of the Subject: on two shells `p ≤ Ω` (the Subject's residues the Carrier's residues below `p`), every label `1 ≤ θ ≤ p − 2` reads back as the integer `θ` in both frames, the point `2⁻¹ + ηθ` has trace one in both with the half-turn as its real part, and it is the readout of a nontrivial mode in both: the Subject's zero at `θ` and the Carrier's zero at `θ` are one zero.

B14.name: FRC.Horizon.norm_ne_zero_on_line
B14.doc: 20:B14 — on the critical line the norm does not vanish when `ν` is a nonsquare: `N(z) = c² − ν θ²` with `c = 2⁻¹`, and `c² = ν θ²` forces `θ = c = 0` (`aniso_tx`), against `Tr z = 2c = 1`.

B14.name: FRC.Horizon.cayley_norm_one
B14.doc: 20:B14 (ii) — the Cayley image of a point of nonzero norm has norm one: `N(w) = N(z)^{2(p−2)} N(z)^2 = 1`; on the critical line every point has a Cayley image on the unit circle `U_{p+1}` (`norm_ne_zero_on_line`).

B14.name: FRC.Horizon.cayley_centre
B14.doc: 20:B14 (iii) — the centre `2⁻¹` goes to `1`: the readout of the label `0` is the real point `2⁻¹`, of norm `4⁻¹`, and its Cayley image is `N^{p−2} · N = 1`.

B14.name: FRC.Horizon.cayley_ne_neg_one
B14.doc: 20:B14 — the Cayley image of a point of the critical line is never `−1`: `w · (1 − z) = z` with `w = −1` reads `−1 + z = z`, so `−1 = 0`.

B14.name: FRC.Horizon.cayley_injective
B14.doc: 20:B14 — the Cayley map is injective on the critical line: two points with one image `w` satisfy `z · (1 − z') = w · (1 − z) · (1 − z') = z' · (1 − z)`, whose coordinates reduce to `z = z'`.

B14.name: FRC.Horizon.cayley_conj
B14.doc: 20:B14 (iv) — the conjugation becomes the inversion: the Cayley image of `z̄` is the conjugate of the Cayley image of `z`, and on the circle the conjugate is the inverse, `w · w̄ = 1`.

E12.name: FRC.Rh.shift_power_character
E12.doc: 20:E12, 20:E15 — the power characters under the drive, the modes its eigenvectors with eigenvalue `g^k` (20-rh's name; the theorem is `FRC.Horizon.shift_power_character`, LM26; the row 20:E1 that first cited it is retired).

E12.name: FRC.Rh.shift_trace
E12.doc: 20:E12, 20:E1 — the fixed-point count of the scale-shift (20-rh's name; the theorem is `FRC.Horizon.shift_trace`, LM26).

E12.name: FRC.Rh.Ext.readout_on_line
E12.doc: 20:E12 (ii) — every readout on the trace-one line (20-rh's name; the theorem is `FRC.Horizon.readout_on_line`, LM26).

E12.name: FRC.Rh.Ext.readout_slot_index
E12.doc: 20:E12 — the slot index of a nontrivial slot (20-rh's name; the theorem is `FRC.Horizon.readout_slot_index`, LM26).

E12.name: FRC.Horizon.mode_expansion
E12.doc: 20:E12 (i), Z10 — every vector on the cycle expands in the power modes: at the point `x = g^j`, `v_j = Σ_{k<p−1} c_k x^k`, the constant mode `k = 0` and the nonterminal modes `0 < k < p − 1`.

E12.name: FRC.Horizon.inversion_res
E12.doc: 20:E14, 20:E12 (i) — the inversion on the residues: `w(y) = −Σ_{k<p−1} ŵ(k) y^{−k}` with `y^{−1} = y^{p−2}`, the sign the self-pairing `−1` of the power characters (`geom_sum_unit`).

E13.name: FRC.Horizon.parseval_cycle
E13.doc: 20:E12 (ii), 20:E13 — the Parseval identity on the cycle: `Σ_{k<n} v̂(k) c_k = Σ_{l<n} v_l²` with `c_k = −v̂(−k)` the mode coefficient, that is `Σ_k v̂(k) v̂(−k) = −Σ_l v_l²`: the finite Parseval identity of the cycle, the self-pairing `−1` of the power characters in place of the complex norm.

E14.name: FRC.Horizon.transform_square
E14.doc: 20:E14, 20:E12 (iv) — the transform's square is the parity: `(W²)_{jl} = Σ_k g^{jk} g^{kl}` is `−1` when `j + l ≡ 0` and `0` otherwise, `W² = −J`; with `F = iW` and `i² = −1`, `F² = J` and `F⁴ = 1` (6:B5).

E14.name: FRC.Horizon.geom_sum_unit
E14.doc: 20:E14 — the geometric sum of a nonzero residue over the cycle, the self-pairing of the modes: `Σ_{k<p−1} u^k` is `−1` when `u = 1` and `0` otherwise.

E14.name: FRC.Horizon.inversion_res
E14.doc: 20:E14, 20:E12 (i) — the inversion on the residues: `w(y) = −Σ_{k<p−1} ŵ(k) y^{−k}` with `y^{−1} = y^{p−2}`, the sign the self-pairing `−1` of the power characters (`geom_sum_unit`).

E14.name: FRC.Horizon.explicit_formula_meridian
E14.doc: 20:E14 — the explicit formula along the meridian: for `x ≤ p − 1` the count of `w` over the positions `1, …, x` is the mode sum, `Σ_{y≤x} w(y) = −Σ_{k<p−1} ŵ(k) S_k(x)`, and the constant mode's read is the main term, `S_0(x) = x`.

E14.name: FRC.Horizon.explicit_formula_cycle
E14.doc: 20:E14, 20:E12 (v) — the explicit formula on the cycle: the count of `v` over the first `x` points of the cycle is the mode sum, `Σ_{j<x} v_j = Σ_{k<n} c_k S_k(x)` with `S_k(x) = Σ_{j<x} (g^j)^k` the cumulative read of the mode `k`, and the constant mode's read is the main term, `S_0(x) = x`.

E15.name: FRC.Rh.shift_power_character
E15.doc: 20:E12, 20:E15 — the power characters under the drive, the modes its eigenvectors with eigenvalue `g^k` (20-rh's name; the theorem is `FRC.Horizon.shift_power_character`, LM26; the row 20:E1 that first cited it is retired).

E15.name: FRC.Horizon.drive_orthogonal
E15.doc: 20:E15 (i) — the drive is orthogonal for the pairing `⟨v, w⟩ = Σ_{l<n} v_l w_l` of the cycle: with the vectors read on the phases (`v_l` the value at `g^l`), the drive `x ↦ g x` is `(Dv)_l = v_{l+1}` and its inverse `(D⁻¹w)_l = w_{l−1}`, and `⟨Dv, w⟩ = ⟨v, D⁻¹w⟩`; `n = p − 1`, the indices mod `n`.

E15.name: FRC.Horizon.spectrum_simple
E15.doc: 20:E15 (ii) — the spectrum of the drive is simple: the eigenvalues `g^0, …, g^{n−1}` of the `n` modes are distinct (`pow_inj`, 26:B3); with `shift_power_character` (the modes are eigenvectors, `D x^k = g^k x^k`) the spectrum is the `n = p − 1` nonzero residues, each once.

E15.name: FRC.Horizon.readout_eigen
E15.doc: 20:E15 (iv) — the readout is the spectral map: the mode `k` is read on the critical line at the label `−g^k`, minus its eigenvalue under the drive.

E15.name: FRC.Horizon.half_turn_negates
E15.doc: 20:E15 (v), 20:B12 — the half-turn of the cycle negates the eigenvalue: `g^{k+π} = −g^k`, `π = 2κ`; the labels of the critical line are the time domain read from `−1 = g^π` (Proposition line (v)).

E15.name: FRC.Horizon.modes_isotropic
E15.doc: 20:E15 (iii) — the modes are isotropic for the pairing: the self-pairing of the mode `k`, `Σ_{l<n} (g^l)^k (g^l)^k = Σ_{l<n} (g^{2k})^l`, vanishes when `g^{2k} ≠ 1` (`mode_square_ne_one`: every mode but `0` and `π`); so the reality of the spectrum is not a consequence of the orthogonality, it is the drive being a scaling by a residue.

F7.name: FRC.Horizon.closure
F7.doc: 20:F7, the foundation clauses of Theorem closure. (i) The wrap of the height reading: a height `T + p` reads as the residue `T` on the cycle of the shell of cardinality `p`, and the successor reaches every residue of the cycle from `0` within `p` steps (00:A5, `successor_cycle`). (ii) Finitude: a reading of capacity `Ω` embeds the registered heights in the shell of `Ω` members (00:A2, `registered_finite`). (iii) Observation: a reading of `o < Ω` states identifies two residues of the Carrier's cycle, and a reading that identifies none has `Ω ≤ o` (00:A4, `observer_part`, `complete_needs_whole`). No axioms.

F7.name: FRC.Horizon.closure_lab
F7.doc: 20:F7, 20:F2, the laboratory instances: for each laboratory Carrier `Ω = 233, 30089, 2408561` (prime, `≡ 1 mod 4`) the largest admissible Subject `p* = 13, 173, 1549` — a prime `p = 4κ + 1` with `κ > 1` and `p² < Ω`, no admissible Subject between `p*` and `√Ω` (`largestSubject`) — so every embedded Subject's cycle is shorter than the Carrier's and the Carrier's top cell is read from labels up to `√Ω`, beyond every embedded window `√p*`. The largest prime below `√Ω` is not in general a Subject: on `Ω = 401` it is `19`, against the Subject `17`; and `Ω = 13` has no admissible Subject. Primality by trial division to the root (`isPrime_of_bounded`), the bounded quantifiers decided by the kernel.

F10.name: FRC.Horizon.invariant_lines
F10.doc: 20:B9, 20:F10, the invariant-line form — the affine lines of the extension are `H_b = {Im z = b}` (`p` lines) and `S_{c,a} = {Re z = a + c·Im z}` (`p²` lines). Conjugation keeps `H_b` exactly when `b = 0` (the meridian) and `S_{c,a}` exactly when `c = 0` (the lines of direction `η`); the half-turn keeps `H_b` exactly when `b = 0` and `S_{c,a}` exactly when `a = 2⁻¹` (the lines through the centre). Hence a line kept by both is the meridian `H_0` or the critical line `S_{0,2⁻¹}`: exactly two.

F10.name: FRC.Horizon.off_line_unregistered
F10.doc: 20:F10 (iii) — a point of the framed plane off both lines (`Im z ≠ 0` and `Re z ≠ 2⁻¹`) lies on no line kept by both involutions: a horizontal line `H_b` through it kept by both has `b = 0`, against `Im z ≠ 0`; a line `S_{c,a}` through it kept by both has `c = 0` and `a = 2⁻¹`, so `Re z = 2⁻¹`, against the hypothesis. The clause of Theorem noline that the python check A18 tests point by point, derived from `invariant_lines`.

F10.name: FRC.Horizon.line_coincidence_all
F10.doc: 20:B13, 20:F10 — frame coincidence on the critical line for every zero of the Subject: on two shells `p ≤ Ω` (the Subject's residues the Carrier's residues below `p`), every label `1 ≤ θ ≤ p − 2` reads back as the integer `θ` in both frames, the point `2⁻¹ + ηθ` has trace one in both with the half-turn as its real part, and it is the readout of a nontrivial mode in both: the Subject's zero at `θ` and the Carrier's zero at `θ` are one zero.

F10.name: FRC.Horizon.mode_at_label
F10.doc: 20:B13, 20:F10 — every label other than `0` and `−1` is the readout of a nontrivial mode: `θ ≠ 0, −1` is `−g^k` for some `1 ≤ k ≤ p − 2`; the label `−1` carries the constant mode `k = 0` and `0` is the centre.

F10.name: FRC.Horizon.readout_on_line
F10.doc: 20:E12 (iii), 20:B12 (i), 20:F10, Z10 — every readout lies on the self-dual line `Tr z = 1`, its real part the half-turn `2⁻¹ = 2κ + 1`, and `θ ↦ z(θ)` is injective: no off-line mode.
